correctness.rationale: For a caterpillar spine of k≥3 vertices, exactly one interior vertex j has zero pendant leaves, all others have ≥1. Each positive-leaf support block contributes U_t=x(1+x)^t+x^t. The bare vertex j can be chosen or unchosen; subtract exactly one forbidden term x^(a+c) (when j and both neighboring supports are absent), giving Q=(1+x)U_aU_c-x^(a+c). U_t is hole-free log-concave. Because the full product P=(1+x)U_aU_c is log-concave, decreasing only coefficient at degree s=a+c can threaten its Turán inequality only at degree s. The explicit integer polynomial for 144(q_s²-q_(s-1)q_(s+1)) has a positive lower bound using ac≤(a+c)²/4 for all positive a,c; thus Q log-concave. Convolution of such sequences preserves log-concavity. An independently implemented sympy coefficient check confirmed 64 a,c≤8 exact margin identities and all Q inequalities, but the symbolic bound supplies the unlimited proof.
